title: The effect of oxytocin on attention to angry and happy faces in chronic depression

citation.title: The effect of oxytocin on attention to angry and happy faces in chronic depression

printed_heading.text: RESEARCH ARTICLE Open Access The effect of oxytocin on attention to angry and happy faces in chronic depression Gregor Domes1,2* , Claus Normann3† and Markus Heinrichs1,2†

what_it_measured.text: We therefore investigated whether oxytocin modulates attention to emotional faces in patients with chronic depression.

dose.text: After completing demographic, clinical and mood-state questionnaires, patients self-administered 6 puffs of Syntocinon® nasal spray (Novartis, Basel, Switzerland; 3 puffs per nostril, containing 4 IU oxytocin each) or a placebo under the supervision of the experimenter.

route.text: Experimental procedures After completing demographic, clinical and mood-state questionnaires, patients self-administered 6 puffs of Syntocinon® nasal spray (Novartis, Basel, Switzerland; 3 puffs per nostril, containing 4 IU oxytocin each) or a placebo under the supervision of the experimenter.

endpoint.text: We assessed reaction times to neutral probes presented at the location of one of two faces depicting happy, angry, or neutral expressions as a prime.
RTs were measured from the onset of the dot probe which followed the primes until the button press

reported_results.text: The four-way ANOVA revealed a significant main effect of prime duration, indicating overall shorter RTs on primes with longer duration (F[2,82] = 16.83; p < .001; η2part = .291).

Although we noted a significant reduction in calmness, wakefulness, and mood over the course of the experiment (all p < .05), this effect did not substantially differ between the oxytocin and placebo group (all p > .10).

Follow-up two-way ANOVAs with the factors group and prime duration confirmed the differential effect of oxytocin with happy and angry faces: for happy faces a significant prime duration by drug interaction was observed, (F[2,82] = 3.21; p = .046; η2part = .073), while there was no significant effect in association with the angry faces (F[2,82] = 0.08; p = .992).
was no such effect in the follow-up ANOVA for happy faces (F[2,82] = 1.87; p = .161), suggesting reduced allocation of attention with increasing duration of the angry prime after oxytocin treatment.

In the allocation scores, we noted significant interaction between prime duration and drug condition (F[2,82] = 3.54; p = .033; η2part = .080): For both happy and angry faces, the placebo group displayed a greater initial allocation of attention with increasing duration of the salient emotional prime, while the oxytocin group demonstrated decreased initial allocation towards the emotional prime with increasing prime duration (Fig. 2a).
